message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is found in the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, a group of placental mammals that split off from other mammalian lineages roughly 55–60 million years ago during the Paleogene period. This ancestor would have been a small, insectivorous mammal that lived on the ancient supercontinent Laurasia.
